# assertr

![assertr logo](https://thepolygram.com/assertrlogo.png)

assertr logo

### What is it?

The assertr package supplies a suite of functions designed to verify
assumptions about data early in an analysis pipeline so that data errors
are spotted early and can be addressed quickly.

This package does not need to be used with the magrittr/dplyr piping
mechanism but the examples in this README use them for clarity.

### Installation

You can install the latest version on CRAN like this

``` r

    install.packages("assertr")
```

or you can install the bleeding-edge development version like this:

``` r

    install.packages("devtools")
    devtools::install_github("ropensci/assertr")
```

### What does it look like?

This package offers five assertion functions, `assert`, `verify`,
`insist`, `assert_rows`, and `insist_rows`, that are designed to be used
shortly after data-loading in an analysis pipeline…

Let’s say, for example, that the R’s built-in car dataset, `mtcars`, was
not built-in but rather procured from an external source that was known
for making errors in data entry or coding. Pretend we wanted to find the
average miles per gallon for each number of engine cylinders. We might
want to first, confirm - that it has the columns “mpg”, “vs”, and “am” -
that the dataset contains more than 10 observations - that the column
for ‘miles per gallon’ (mpg) is a positive number - that the column for
‘miles per gallon’ (mpg) does not contain a datum that is outside 4
standard deviations from its mean, and - that the am and vs columns
(automatic/manual and v/straight engine, respectively) contain 0s and 1s
only - each row contains at most 2 NAs - each row is unique *jointly*
between the “mpg”, “am”, and “wt” columns - each row’s mahalanobis
distance is within 10 median absolute deviations of all the distances
(for outlier detection)

This could be written (in order) using `assertr` like this:

``` r

    library(dplyr)
    library(assertr)

    mtcars %>%
      verify(has_all_names("mpg", "vs", "am", "wt")) %>%
      verify(nrow(.) > 10) %>%
      verify(mpg > 0) %>%
      insist(within_n_sds(4), mpg) %>%
      assert(in_set(0,1), am, vs) %>%
      assert_rows(num_row_NAs, within_bounds(0,2), everything()) %>%
      assert_rows(col_concat, is_uniq, mpg, am, wt) %>%
      insist_rows(maha_dist, within_n_mads(10), everything()) %>%
      group_by(cyl) %>%
      summarise(avg.mpg=mean(mpg))
```

If any of these assertions were violated, an error would have been
raised and the pipeline would have been terminated early.

Let’s see what the error message look like when you chain a bunch of
failing assertions together.

``` r
    > mtcars %>%
    +   chain_start %>%
    +   assert(in_set(1, 2, 3, 4), carb) %>%
    +   assert_rows(rowMeans, within_bounds(0,5), gear:carb) %>%
    +   verify(nrow(.)==10) %>%
    +   verify(mpg < 32) %>%
    +   chain_end
    There are 7 errors across 4 verbs:
    -
             verb redux_fn           predicate     column index value
    1      assert     <NA>  in_set(1, 2, 3, 4)       carb    30   6.0
    2      assert     <NA>  in_set(1, 2, 3, 4)       carb    31   8.0
    3 assert_rows rowMeans within_bounds(0, 5) ~gear:carb    30   5.5
    4 assert_rows rowMeans within_bounds(0, 5) ~gear:carb    31   6.5
    5      verify     <NA>       nrow(.) == 10       <NA>     1    NA
    6      verify     <NA>            mpg < 32       <NA>    18    NA
    7      verify     <NA>            mpg < 32       <NA>    20    NA

    Error: assertr stopped execution
```

### What does `assertr` give me?

- `verify` - takes a data frame (its first argument is provided by the
  `%>%` operator above), and a logical (boolean) expression. Then,
  `verify` evaluates that expression using the scope of the provided
  data frame. If any of the logical values of the expression’s result
  are `FALSE`, `verify` will raise an error that terminates any further
  processing of the pipeline.

- `assert` - takes a data frame, a predicate function, and an arbitrary
  number of columns to apply the predicate function to. The predicate
  function (a function that returns a logical/boolean value) is then
  applied to every element of the columns selected, and will raise an
  error if it finds any violations. Internally, the `assert` function
  uses `dplyr`’s `select` function to extract the columns to test the
  predicate function on.

- `insist` - takes a data frame, a predicate-generating function, and an
  arbitrary number of columns. For each column, the the
  predicate-generating function is applied, returning a predicate. The
  predicate is then applied to every element of the columns selected,
  and will raise an error if it finds any violations. The reason for
  using a predicate-generating function to return a predicate to use
  against each value in each of the selected rows is so that, for
  example, bounds can be dynamically generated based on what the data
  look like; this the only way to, say, create bounds that check if each
  datum is within x z-scores, since the standard deviation isn’t known a
  priori. Internally, the `insist` function uses `dplyr`’s `select`
  function to extract the columns to test the predicate function on.

- `assert_rows` - takes a data frame, a row reduction function, a
  predicate function, and an arbitrary number of columns to apply the
  predicate function to. The row reduction function is applied to the
  data frame, and returns a value for each row. The predicate function
  is then applied to every element of vector returned from the row
  reduction function, and will raise an error if it finds any
  violations. This functionality is useful, for example, in conjunction
  with the
  [`num_row_NAs()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/num_row_NAs.md)
  function to ensure that there is below a certain number of missing
  values in each row. Internally, the `assert_rows` function uses
  `dplyr`’s`select` function to extract the columns to test the
  predicate function on.

- `insist_rows` - takes a data frame, a row reduction function, a
  predicate-generating function, and an arbitrary number of columns to
  apply the predicate function to. The row reduction function is applied
  to the data frame, and returns a value for each row. The
  predicate-generating function is then applied to the vector returned
  from the row reduction function and the resultant predicate is applied
  to each element of that vector. It will raise an error if it finds any
  violations. This functionality is useful, for example, in conjunction
  with the
  [`maha_dist()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/maha_dist.md)
  function to ensure that there are no flagrant outliers. Internally,
  the `assert_rows` function uses `dplyr`’s`select` function to extract
  the columns to test the predicate function on.

`assertr` also offers four (so far) predicate functions designed to be
used with the `assert` and `assert_rows` functions:

- `not_na` - that checks if an element is not NA
- `within_bounds` - that returns a predicate function that checks if a
  numeric value falls within the bounds supplied, and
- `in_set` - that returns a predicate function that checks if an element
  is a member of the set supplied. (also allows inverse for “not in
  set”)
- `is_uniq` - that checks to see if each element appears only once

and predicate generators designed to be used with the `insist` and
`insist_rows` functions:

- `within_n_sds` - used to dynamically create bounds to check vector
  elements with based on standard z-scores
- `within_n_mads` - better method for dynamically creating bounds to
  check vector elements with based on ‘robust’ z-scores (using median
  absolute deviation)

and the following row reduction functions designed to be used with
`assert_rows` and `insist_rows`:

- `num_row_NAs` - counts number of missing values in each row
- `maha_dist` - computes the mahalanobis distance of each row (for
  outlier detection). It will coerce categorical variables into numerics
  if it needs to.
- `col_concat` - concatenates all rows into strings
- `duplicated_across_cols` - checking if a row contains a duplicated
  value across columns

and, finally, some other utilities for use with `verify`

- `has_all_names` - check if the data frame or list has all supplied
  names
- `has_only_names` - check that a data frame or list have *only* the
  names requested
- `has_class` - checks if passed data has a particular class

### More info

For more info, check out the `assertr` vignette

``` r
    > vignette("assertr")
```

Or [read it
here](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=assertr/vignettes/assertr.html)

# Package index

## All functions

- [`assert()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/assert.md) :
  Raises error if predicate is FALSE in any columns selected
- [`assert_rows()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/assert_rows.md)
  : Raises error if predicate is FALSE for any row after applying row
  reduction function
- [`assertr`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/assertr.md)
  [`assertr-package`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/assertr.md)
  : assertr: Assertive programming for R analysis pipeline.
- [`chain_start()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/chaining_functions.md)
  [`chain_end()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/chaining_functions.md)
  : Chaining functions
- [`col_concat()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/col_concat.md)
  : Concatenate all columns of each row in data frame into a string
- [`duplicates_across_cols()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/duplicates_across_cols.md)
  : Checks if row contains at least one value duplicated in its column
- [`generate_id()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/generate_id.md)
  : Generates random ID string
- [`has_all_names()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/has_all_names.md)
  : Returns TRUE if data.frame or list has specified names
- [`has_class()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/has_class.md)
  : Returns TRUE if data.frame columns have a specified class
- [`has_only_names()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/has_only_names.md)
  : Returns TRUE if data.frame or list has only the specified names
- [`in_set()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/in_set.md) :
  Returns TRUE if value in set
- [`insist()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/insist.md) :
  Raises error if dynamically created predicate is FALSE in any columns
  selected
- [`insist_rows()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/insist_rows.md)
  : Raises error if dynamically created predicate is FALSE for any row
  after applying row reduction function
- [`is_uniq()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/is_uniq.md)
  : Returns TRUE where no elements appear more than once
- [`maha_dist()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/maha_dist.md)
  : Computes mahalanobis distance for each row of data frame
- [`not_na()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/not_na.md) :
  Returns TRUE if value is not NA
- [`num_row_NAs()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/num_row_NAs.md)
  : Counts number of NAs in each row
- [`print(`*`<assertr_assert_error>`*`)`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/print.assertr_assert_error.md)
  : Printing assertr's assert errors
- [`print(`*`<assertr_defect>`*`)`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/print.assertr_defect.md)
  : Printing assertr's defect
- [`print(`*`<assertr_success>`*`)`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/print.assertr_success.md)
  : Printing assertr's success
- [`print(`*`<assertr_verify_error>`*`)`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/print.assertr_verify_error.md)
  : Printing assertr's verify errors
- [`success_logical()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/success_and_error_functions.md)
  [`success_continue()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/success_and_error_functions.md)
  [`success_append()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/success_and_error_functions.md)
  [`success_report()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/success_and_error_functions.md)
  [`success_df_return()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/success_and_error_functions.md)
  [`error_stop()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/success_and_error_functions.md)
  [`just_warn()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/success_and_error_functions.md)
  [`error_report()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/success_and_error_functions.md)
  [`warn_report()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/success_and_error_functions.md)
  [`error_append()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/success_and_error_functions.md)
  [`warning_append()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/success_and_error_functions.md)
  [`error_return()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/success_and_error_functions.md)
  [`error_df_return()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/success_and_error_functions.md)
  [`error_logical()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/success_and_error_functions.md)
  [`defect_append()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/success_and_error_functions.md)
  [`defect_report()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/success_and_error_functions.md)
  [`defect_df_return()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/success_and_error_functions.md)
  : Success and error functions
- [`summary(`*`<assertr_assert_error>`*`)`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/summary.assertr_assert_error.md)
  : Summarizing assertr's assert errors
- [`summary(`*`<assertr_verify_error>`*`)`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/summary.assertr_verify_error.md)
  : Summarizing assertr's verify errors
- [`verify()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/verify.md) :
  Raises error if expression is FALSE anywhere
- [`within_bounds()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/within_bounds.md)
  : Creates bounds checking predicate
- [`within_n_mads()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/within_n_mads.md)
  : Return a function to create robust z-score checking predicate
- [`within_n_sds()`](https://docs.ropensci.org/assertr/reference/within_n_sds.md)
  : Return a function to create z-score checking predicate
